guides.name: Get a grease or oil stain out of clothes
steps: Blot up extra oil with a clean paper towel. Do not rub.
Sprinkle cornstarch or talcum powder on the spot to soak up oil, then brush it off.
Rub a little dish soap gently into the stain, then rinse it out.
Rub liquid laundry detergent into the spot and let it sit about 10 minutes.
Put it in the washer without rinsing the detergent off.
Wash it in the hottest water the care label allows.
Check the spot before drying. If you still see it, repeat these steps.
safety: Test soap and detergent on a hidden seam first; they can change the color.
Keep it out of the dryer until the stain is gone; drying sets it.
Treat it soon. Oil stains get darker the longer they sit.
stopIf: The label says dry clean only. Take it to a dry cleaner instead.
It is wool or silk. Only blot and use powder, then wash as the label says; no bleach.
The color changes when you test a hidden seam.

guides.name: Clean dirty tile grout
steps: Open a window or run the fan and put on gloves.
Sweep or rinse off loose dirt first.
Spray the grout cleaner on a small section and let it sit as the label says.
Scrub along the grout lines with the brush.
Rinse with clean water and wipe dry, then move to the next section.
safety: Use one cleaner at a time and never mix it with bleach products.
Rinse well before switching to a different cleaner.
stopIf: Grout is cracked, crumbling or missing.
Tiles are loose or sound hollow when tapped.

sources.title: How to Clean Tile Grout | Lysol US
sources.quote: it’s always best to start with less harsh cleaning products and work your way up if and when needed.

sources.title: Dangers of Mixing Bleach with Cleaners | Washington State Department of Health
sources.quote: Don't mix bleach with ammonia, acids, or other cleaners.
